Here's a summary of everything I did and what you need in App Store Connect:

---

## Changes Made

### 1. Fixed Colors (4 files)
All paywall screens were using `Color.black` backgrounds and green `Color(red: 0.3, green: 0.8, blue: 0.5)` accents. Updated to use your app's `ColorTheme`:

- **Backgrounds**: `Color.black` → `ColorTheme.backgroundGradient` (deep navy)
- **Accent/checkmarks**: Green → `ColorTheme.neonPink` (warm amber-orange)
- **Buttons**: Green gradients → `ColorTheme.primaryGradient` (amber-orange → royal blue)
- **Button text**: `.black` → `.white` (readable on the new gradient)
- **Spin wheel segments**: Black/white → navy theme colors with amber-orange text
- **SpecialOfferView**: Card backgrounds, trial banner, loading states all updated

Files changed: `FeaturesBenefitsView.swift`, `PromoOfferView.swift`, `SpinWheelView.swift`, `SpecialOfferView.swift`

### 2. Added Discounted Plan to StoreKit

Added `com.romirjain.focusflow.premium.yearly.discount` at **$19.99/year** to:
- `DopaFryProducts.storekit` — new subscription entry with 3-day free trial
- `StoreKitManager.swift` — new `annualDiscount` case in `ProductID` enum
- `SpecialOfferView.swift` — now purchases the discounted product instead of the regular annual

---

## What to Add in App Store Connect

In **App Store Connect > Monetization > Subscriptions**, under your **"DopaFry Premium"** subscription group, you need to create these products:

| Reference Name | Product ID | Type | Price | Trial |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DopaFry Weekly | `com.romirjain.focusflow.premium.weekly` | Auto-Renewable | $2.99/week | 3-day free |
| DopaFry Monthly | `com.romirjain.focusflow.premium.monthly` | Auto-Renewable | $7.99/month | 3-day free |
| DopaFry Yearly | `com.romirjain.focusflow.premium.yearly` | Auto-Renewable | $29.99/year | 3-day free |
| **DopaFry Yearly Discount** | **`com.romirjain.focusflow.premium.yearly.discount`** | **Auto-Renewable** | **$19.99/year** | **3-day free** |

And under **In-App Purchases** (non-consumable):

| Reference Name | Product ID | Type | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| DopaFry Lifetime | `com.romirjain.focusflow.premium.lifetime` | Non-Consumable | $149.99 |

### Steps:
1. Go to **Monetization > Subscriptions**
2. Create subscription group **"DopaFry Premium"** if it doesn't exist
3. Add all 4 subscriptions above to that group
4. **Important**: Set the **subscription rank** — the discounted yearly should be at a **lower level** (Level 2) than the regular yearly (Level 1), so users can downgrade to the discount but new users see the regular price first
5. For each subscription, add the **3-day free introductory offer** (Free trial, 3 days, 1 period)
6. Go to **In-App Purchases** and add the Lifetime product as a Non-Consumable
7. For each product, add **localization** (display name + description) and a **review screenshot**

1. **Onboarding**: User picks their "dopamine drain" apps (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, etc.)
2. **Default state**: Those apps are shielded (blocked) — not as punishment, but as "your brain needs a break from these"
3. **Earn to unlock**: Spend DC to unlock a drain app for a timed window (e.g., 15 DC = 15 min of TikTok)
4. **Natural consequence**: When your DC runs out, the shield goes back up. No guilt, no willpower needed — you just ran out of budget

This is fundamentally different from competitors because:
- **ADHD brains rebel against restriction** — "you can't use this" triggers defiance. "You haven't earned this yet" triggers the reward-seeking behavior that ADHD brains are wired for
- **It gamifies self-regulation** — which is literally the core skill ADHD people struggle with
- **It ties into your existing dopamine debt gauge** — high debt = your DC earn rate drops, so you naturally get less screen time when you're overstimulated

## Root Cause
`ViewModelContainer` holds nested `ObservableObject` instances (`coinManager`, `activityTracker`, etc.) as `@Published` properties. But `@Published` on reference types only fires when the *reference itself* is reassigned — NOT when the object's internal properties change. So when `coinManager.earnCoins()` updates `balance` and `todayEarned`, views subscribed to `viewModelContainer` never saw the change.

## Fixes

1. **`ViewModelIntegration.swift`** — Added Combine forwarding so that when any nested ViewModel (coinManager, activityTracker, coachEngine, impulseTracker, dopamineDebt) publishes `objectWillChange`, the container re-publishes it. This means Dashboard, Log tab, and all other views will now re-render when DC balance changes.

2. **`LogTabView.swift:287`** — Changed "DC Earned" stat from summing local `ActivityEvent.dcEarned` (which doesn't include streak multiplier) to reading `viewModelContainer.coinManager.todayEarned` (the actual awarded amount including multiplier).

Now when you log an activity, the DC balance will update everywhere — Dashboard, Log tab stats, and the coin animation overlay.
